name: skill-tasks
_comment: Three tasks that share one procedure (add a focused unit test to an existing file, in that file's own #[cfg(test)] module). The suite exists to answer one question: does an agent write a skill after the first task and reuse it on the next two? Watch the trace for SkillOp events and the report for the skill_* metrics. Live only: the stub implementer writes nothing, so expect_writes tasks cannot pass offline.

tasks.name: test-sanitize
tasks.goal: Add a unit test for the private helper `fn sanitize` in src/eval/runner.rs. That file has no test module yet, so follow the repo's unit-test convention: create one `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block at the end of the file and put the test inside it. The test must call `sanitize("a b/c")` and assert the result is `a-b-c`. Run `cargo test` and make it pass.

tasks.name: test-condense
tasks.goal: Add a unit test to src/engine/orchestrator.rs for `condense_output`. Follow the repo's unit-test convention: the file already has a test module — extend it rather than adding a second `mod tests`. The test must feed condense_output a body containing a line with `FAILED` and a line starting with `Compiling`, then assert the FAILED line survives and the Compiling line is dropped. Run `cargo test` and make it pass.

tasks.name: test-window-on
tasks.goal: Add a unit test to src/context/retriever.rs for the public helper `window_on`. That file has no test module yet, so follow the repo's unit-test convention: create one `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block and put the test inside it. The test must assert that window_on returns a short input unchanged. Run `cargo test` and make it pass.
